text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: P1 INCIDENT — KV cache amplification detected in us-west-2. Batching error rate spike +22%, p95>2.8s. Paging oncall.

sara: Ack. joining. pulling dashboards and logs now. wavefront: https://wave.front/reds/kvcache?window=5m

mike: Noting recent rollouts to batching flags in prod. Could be per-tenant window increase or microbatch parameter.

ops-bot: Auto-sampled log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T04:02:41Z ERROR kv_cache shard=22 mem=13.2GB evictions=98k
2026-03-15T04:02:42Z INFO batching config tenant=beta-xyz window=2048
```

anya: I see an LD change: flag=batch_window target=tenant:acme_inc override set at 03:58 UTC by olivia — env=prod. It was intended for staging.

kevin: acme_inc accounts for ~10-14% of us-west-2 traffic; their typical seq_len distribution is heavy-tailed which will blow kv memory with large window.

sara: Symptoms: continuous-batching queue depth rising, region serving nodes cpu 92%, errors: 'kv cache OOM' and batching timeouts. We need emergency revert + immediate shedding.

olivia: Confirmed — that was my change run as part of a performance check. I mis-targeted the flag to prod. Rolling it back now.

mike: While rollback runs, apply emergency routing shed to acme_inc to protect platform: set tenant_rate_cap to 25rps and enable queue-timeout to 250ms for that slice.

anya: Throttle command executed:
```
POST /internal/routing/shed
{"tenant":"acme_inc","cap_rps":25,"queue_timeout_ms":250}
```
Routing logs: shed active. Dropped 20% of acme_inc requests; observed immediate drop in kv page reads.

ops-bot: LaunchDarkly rollback job started (id=5913). Estimated 45s.

kevin: Checking cache metrics: eviction rate halving on canary hosts. But global tail still high — some shards lagging.

sara: Suggest we roll a micro-canary of default window to 15% hosts in the region and keep per-tenant throttle for 30 minutes. Also create a temporary graceful-fallback: route heavy seq_len requests to a cpu-optimized pool with lower kv caching.

mike: I'll spin up a fallback pool (tag=fallback-seqlen) and add a routing rule: if seq_len>1024 route->fallback. Deploying now.

olivia: Rollback completed. Flag state restored to 512 for acme_inc.

ops-bot: Canary rollout: hosts tagged batch-window-default (count=10). Monitoring window=10m.

sara: Early telemetry: canary hosts stable, 60% fewer evictions, p95 down to 540ms. Fallback pool absorbing ~3% of requests, which helps.

kevin: Customer-facing impact: ACME's chat feature had 10-12% error rate during window; estimate affected sessions ~6.5k. SLA window ~13m. Notify CS and accounts.

olivia: Messaging drafted and sent to account team. I'll lead outreach and apologize for incident. Scheduling immediate postmortem with ACME PM.

mike: Handoff: oncall -> eng-sre. I'll stay for watch 45m. eng-sre (kevin) to lead remediation tasks and coordinate runbook updates.

anya: Filed follow-ups:
- INC-2026-45: postmortem + timeline
- TASK-5021: LD guardrails — prevent staging flags targeting prod
- TASK-5022: flag preflight approval for per-tenant overrides
- TASK-5023: routing prechecks for seq_len-based routing

ops-bot: Incident marked mitigated. Snapshot: error delta +0.7%, p95 normalized. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-amplify

kevin: We'll patch the LD workflow to require explicit prod-scope ops approval for batch-window overrides, and add automated detection of large-window flips to prod with alerting.

sara: Great work. Closing after 45m steady-state watch. Leaving notes in PagerDuty.

mike: Thanks team. :thumbsup:
